perceptions.customer_perception: Players expect and even embrace brutal, repeated PvP deaths right from spawn, but describe it as demoralizing when it happens over and over with no recourse.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Marketing does reference danger from 'other survivors' and starting 'armed only with a rock and a torch' (M024, M027), framing death as part of the core survival fantasy.
perceptions.recommended_action: Keep leaning into the danger-of-other-players fantasy, but pair it with messaging that sets expectations about the learning curve so new players aren't blindsided.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Every death is a story: even the pros started naked on the beach.
perceptions.evidence_quote: A naked comes over and starts bashing me with a rock.

perceptions.customer_perception: Players see Rust as an all-consuming time investment that can border on unhealthy addiction, with huge effort lost in seconds.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Marketing hints at this via 'do whatever it takes to last another night' (M003) but never acknowledges the scale of time investment or grind-to-loss ratio.
perceptions.recommended_action: Add honest messaging or onboarding tips about time investment and pacing (e.g., solo/casual server modes, offline protection features) to manage expectations and reduce burnout-driven negative reviews.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Big risks, bigger stories — but we've got tools to help you play on your own schedule.
perceptions.evidence_quote: I shouldn't have to spend 10 hours to build a base, just for it to be torn down in 15 seconds by no-lifes who have rocket launchers 4 hours after wipe, when I don't even have enough cloth to make clothes or low grade fuel to make a furnace.

perceptions.customer_perception: Playing with friends and the rare moments of genuine community warmth are treasured highlights that keep players attached to the game, despite the harsh world.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Only touched in passing via 'Cooperate with friends, make alliances' (M035) and server modding support (M008) — a 20% coverage overlap and effectively a hidden strength.
perceptions.recommended_action: Elevate co-op and community stories in marketing creative — testimonials, trailers of friend groups building/surviving together — since this is a strong, underused positive signal.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Rust is better with friends: build trust, build bases, build memories.
perceptions.evidence_quote: Super fun and chill, best to play with friends. We've just finished our base and immediately our neighbor from a very big clan send us a dozen of rocket launcher as a welcoming home present. What a lovely community!

perceptions.customer_perception: Base building, crafting, and electrical/automation systems are seen as deeply satisfying creative outlets that mesh well with the survival and PvP loop.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Strongly and accurately marketed via 'Base Building and Raiding' (M011), 'Design and build bases' (M029), and 'Complex electrical, farming, and automation systems' (M014).
perceptions.recommended_action: Keep current building/engineering marketing as-is; it matches player enthusiasm closely.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: From a single shack to a fortress with automated defenses — build whatever you can imagine.
perceptions.evidence_quote: The building, crafting, exploration, and PvP all work really well together.

perceptions.customer_perception: A notable share of players describe genuine emotional distress, rage, and mental-health strain from the game's punishing loop, beyond typical 'hardcore' framing.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Marketing does not address this at all; it only implies difficulty via 'everything wants you to die' (M002) without acknowledging the emotional toll players report.
perceptions.recommended_action: Do not market the distress itself, but invest in and message quality-of-life/anti-toxicity features, and moderate messaging tone so it doesn't glamorize the misery some players report.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Intense by design, but we're building tools to keep the challenge fun, not exhausting.
perceptions.evidence_quote: Made me want to rip my skin off, the only way to play this game is if your a soulless, dirty, dishonest, slimy, depressed loser with no life, who makes it their mission to make the people with lives outside of this pos game a miserable time and completely unenjoyable.

perceptions.customer_perception: Players frequently encounter toxic, abusive behavior including slurs from other players, which is a major undercurrent of the community experience despite occasional praise for friendliness.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Essentially absent from marketing (only 9% vocabulary overlap with M008); the 'watch out for other survivors' framing glosses over verbal abuse specifically.
perceptions.recommended_action: Add visible messaging about moderation tools, reporting systems, and curated/managed server options to reassure prospective players concerned about toxicity.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Danger comes from raiders, not hate speech — explore our moderated and community-run server options.
perceptions.evidence_quote: This game is cancerous and instead of trying to implement meaningful changes to help take the edge off the toxicity, the developers actively embrace it.

perceptions.customer_perception: Choosing the right server (official vs modded, PvE vs PvP) is confusing and frustrating, and admin/server quality varies wildly, impacting first impressions.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Only loosely covered via 'Host your own servers and with server-side modding support' (M009), which doesn't help players choose or understand server types.
perceptions.recommended_action: Add a clear server-selection guide or in-marketing explainer (official vs community, PvE vs PvP, wipe schedules) to reduce onboarding friction highlighted by players.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Thousands of servers, one perfect fit — find your ideal Rust experience with our server guide.
perceptions.evidence_quote: (This is at least in my experience in official and 2x servers) Are there any good pve servers that aren't modded to where it doesn't feel like vanilla Rust anymore?

perceptions.customer_perception: Survival mechanics like hunger, environment, and wildlife are enjoyed and seen as core to the appeal, even when brutal.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Well covered by 'brave environmental dangers... build a shelter, eat (or be eaten)' (M025) and the overall SURVIVE pillar (M032).
perceptions.recommended_action: Keep current survival-focused marketing; it accurately reflects what players enjoy.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Hunt, gather, and survive against nature itself — the wild island doesn't go easy on anyone.
perceptions.evidence_quote: LOVE THIS GAME. I have died to so many animals but it is so worth it. i would die a million times to all kinds of animals if it meant I would continue playing this game forever. Discovered I am the hunter AND the gatherer. 10/10

perceptions.customer_perception: Performance issues, crashes, and poor optimization (especially on lower-end hardware and Mac/Linux) are a persistent frustration undermining the polished graphics marketing.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Marketing touts a 'massive recent graphics upgrade and environment overhaul' (M018) without addressing performance/stability concerns raised by many players.
perceptions.recommended_action: Reduce heavy emphasis on graphics-upgrade messaging until optimization improves, or pair it with concrete performance benchmarks/system requirements transparency.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Stunning visuals, tuned for real-world rigs — see our recommended settings guide for smooth performance.
perceptions.evidence_quote: my pc used to be able to run this i lowered my graphics now it cant.

perceptions.customer_perception: Raiding and losing hard-earned loot (especially offline raiding) is a core love/hate mechanic that defines the endgame tension.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Directly and accurately marketed: 'raiding their bases and taking their hard-won goods' (M036), 'Base Building and Raiding' (M011).
perceptions.recommended_action: Keep raiding messaging, but consider highlighting offline-protection or base-defense tools to address the specific pain point of offline raids.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Defend what's yours, day or night — build defenses that hold even while you're offline.
perceptions.evidence_quote: Without the depth of interaction, it leads to a gameplay loop that requires significant time investment, just to be offline raided.

perceptions.customer_perception: Solo and small-group players feel structurally disadvantaged against large clans/zergs, even though many value the freedom to choose their playstyle.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Marketing vaguely implies playstyle flexibility through cooperation and alliance language (M035) but doesn't acknowledge the solo-vs-clan balance concern at all.
perceptions.recommended_action: Add messaging or matchmaking/server-tagging features that call out solo-friendly or small-group-friendly servers to support this underserved but vocal segment.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: Solo, duo, or clan — there's a Rust server balanced for your playstyle.
perceptions.evidence_quote: clans dominate, the game is not solo friendly at all but can be fun at the start fo a wipe then no more.

perceptions.customer_perception: Long-time players are frustrated with perceived lazy or misdirected developer priorities, especially around platform support (e.g., Linux) and bug fixes versus cosmetic monetization.
perceptions.current_marketing_position: Marketing heavily promotes update cadence and content volume ('395 content updates', 'guaranteed content patch every month' - M004) but doesn't address platform support or fix prioritization concerns.
perceptions.recommended_action: Reduce pure quantity-of-updates messaging and add transparency around bug-fix priorities and platform support roadmap to rebuild trust.
perceptions.suggested_messaging: More than content drops — real fixes, real platform support, real communication.
perceptions.evidence_quote: Such a bad company add proton support easy anticheat is linux compatable. 4 months ago i can now no longer play on linux, I had respect for facepunch devs but now FO. Useless company. will be asking for refund they do not deserve a penny anymore.

top_recommendations.title: Spotlight friendship and community moments
top_recommendations.detail: Players call out chill, friendly moments with friends as a hidden highlight (69 mentions) that's barely marketed. Feature co-op stories and testimonials in trailers and store page to broaden appeal beyond hardcore PvP fans.

top_recommendations.title: Provide a clear server-selection guide
top_recommendations.detail: Confusion over official vs modded, PvE vs PvP, and solo vs clan servers is a recurring pain point (T007, T011). A simple in-store or in-game guide would reduce onboarding friction and negative first impressions.

top_recommendations.title: Dial back graphics/update-volume bragging until backed by stability
top_recommendations.detail: Heavy emphasis on '395 updates' and graphics overhauls rings hollow next to persistent crash, performance, and platform-support (Linux) complaints. Pair any such claims with concrete fix/optimization commitments.

top_recommendations.title: Acknowledge the toll, don't just glamorize the grind
top_recommendations.detail: Time-sink, rage, and toxicity themes (T002, T005, T006) show real player strain. Reframe messaging away from glorifying addiction toward highlighting quality-of-life tools, moderation, and manageable play options.

top_recommendations.title: Preserve core survival and raiding pillars
top_recommendations.detail: Base building, raiding, and environmental survival mechanics (T004, T008, T010) are strongly aligned with player sentiment and marketing — continue investing here as the brand's proven core.
